11. The remaining claims survive, but now Wayfarer will have to move into specifics: What exactly was shared, when, with who.

Details that after over a year of discovery, they still don't seem to have any certainty about.

10. The breach of contract claims are dismissed with prejudice, meaning Abel won't get another attempt to revive them.

Pour one out for the Van-sham crowd who are doubtless going to spiral over this.

9. The problem for Wayfarer is that we already know this ISNT true, Nathan's own text messages with the Daily Mail show that Sloane's message to Nathan was in response to a reporter reading out Nathan's texts. 

Not Jones sharing the details of Abel's phone.

8. Count 4, defamation per se also survives as again, taken as true, Jones falsely telling Sloane that Wayfarer engaged in a smear campaign as retaliation for sexual harassment complaints, would meet the criteria.

7. Count 3, fair dealing survives as Liman rejects Jones' argument it is duplicative of the breach of contract claims. The Judge arguing that taken as true "sharing of negative information about Wayfarer with Lively" would count, so now Wayfarer must prove that happened.

6. In fact Wayfarer only allege Jones failed to heed their directive to talk to the press, but not only is that not covered by their contract, Wayfarer fail to offer any facts that she DID talk to the press.

5. Their second breach of contract claim for failure to provide services "in a professional manner" also fails, because the contract was with Jonesworks, not Jones herself, alleging a "close and trusting relationship" with Abel, who ran their account

4. But Wayfarer also allege the information disclosed to Sloane is all false, about a smear campaign that never took place.

But it can't both be "false" and "Confidential". Wayfarer's own argument defeats their claims.

3. Liman points out that the definition of Confidential Information" is "carefully drawn" and must be disclosed BY Wayfarer TO Jonesworks. Abel's private communications don't count under that definition.

2. Breach of contract fails in part because Wayfarer does not allege any Confidential Information was actually shared...

... that's a huge blow for those who've been screeching "Van-sham" for the last year. Too bad, so sad.

⚖️Judge Liman rules on Jones' Motion to Dismiss Abel's amended counterclaims⚖️

Granted in part, denied in part. Only two claims survive against Jones... 🧵

5. Hilariously, Wayfarer are also claiming their own deposition testimony, in which they flatly deny any ability to recall their own messages should be entirely inadmissible.

4. Wayfarer are also objecting to the number of trial witnesses Lively has identified: 40.

With 8 defendants and 13 claims, that's less than 10 exhibits per claim per defendant, and 3 witnesses per claim... 

These are far from an excessive amount.

3. This runs entirely counter to Wayfarer's PR campaign of the last 18 months which has claimed Lively has no witnesses and no evidence.

Now, they're complaining Lively intends to bring 1,000 exhibits to trial.

2. Despite working on their pre-trial motions for the last 4 months, Wayfarer are petitioning the court claiming they need an extra week due to "voluminous disclosures" that "exceed the bounds of any conceivable evidentiary presentation".

🚨Wayfarer ask for yet another extension🚨

Wayfarer are asking to push back pre-trial motions by a week, because Lively has too much evidence.

No, seriously.
